supersedes.reason: Independent compiled-browser review found that registered global shortcuts could escape the open modal, repeated help activation could overwrite the original restoration target, and the changing theme action name contradicted aria-pressed. This evidence binds the narrow accessibility remediation and complete regression replay.

checks.result: All 25 commands pass in 502.34 seconds at exact clean commit c3306ff: 148 governed tests, 34 desktop tests, nine package/application/native commands, functional-product browser checks, immutable performance thresholds, 139 reference workflow cases, 390 reference keyboard cases, 64 accessibility/responsive cases, and 64 visual captures. Report SHA-256: da6377103d85f6e2de92ee9c582c5916d49948d6e990ba03debe3bb2b6adaa97.

The compiled product now keeps focus inside the modal for Ctrl+K, Ctrl+/, repeated Ctrl+/, and Alt+H; Escape closes it and restores the original command field. The stable Dark theme toggle name and aria-pressed state track the actual theme. All nine commands, six design-system cases, one functional CAP-01 page, zero reference-only pages, two responsive cases, and zero requests pass. Report SHA-256: a61cb16e8a918082683ba0a0d0aa92fd2e8eef2f9bedd4767b8b5ade24ef17f3.

All seven focused checker tests pass after rebuilding the product manifest, including compiled product accessibility, exact product/reference inventory, unsafe-content denial, and deterministic report boundaries.
All 18 application tests pass across six test files; the application contract asserts the stable theme-toggle name/state and preserves the complete bounded shortcut registry.

evidence: While the modal is open, every registered global shortcut is consumed and focus is returned to its close control; no shortcut can focus the command field or project home behind aria-modal content.

Repeated help activation no longer replaces restoreFocusRef. Escape clears the held reference and restores the original connected element, with the visible shortcut trigger as a safe fallback if that element was removed.

The theme button has the stable accessible name Dark theme. aria-pressed=false means light is active and true means dark is active; the compiled browser asserts the name remains stable across activation and state matches the document theme.
The compiled-browser regression replays Ctrl+K, Ctrl+/, Alt+H, repeated help, Tab, Shift+Tab, and Escape inside one modal session, then requires restoration to the original command field.

The full product replay and focused suite continue to deny reference pages, unexpected requests, stale manifests, unsafe URLs, and output/input inventory drift while all expected keyboard, focus, theme, live-region, and responsive paths pass.

The remediation changes only ApplicationRuntime, its unit contract, the compiled product checker, the immutable original evidence record, and the exact planning review transition; product/reference build separation, native privileges, routes, and approved reference bytes are unchanged.
The exact clean full desktop profile and current UI-change gate pass without documentation, contract, migration, fixture, or audit drift.

reviewerDisposition.note: Independent re-review must reproduce every registered shortcut while the modal is open, repeated help plus Escape restoration, stable theme-toggle naming/state, and the exact seven-file evidence transition before approval.
